description: Blocking validation for zaq-za4.6 and future serving issues. Fresh zaq-za4.6/serving-role worktree: ROLES=serving MIX_ENV=test mix run boots successfully after skipping unused Agent/BO catalogs; ROLES=bo, ROLES=engine and default :all exit 137 within seconds. Manual startup of shared children, FTSBackend.detect_and_cache, ValidModalities.list and ReqLLM.Providers.register! succeeds; process exits 137 precisely at LLMDB.load(ZAQRouter.llmdb_opts()). Isolate environment/memory versus catalog regression without weakening existing BO/Agent behavior. Preserve validation via normal full application startup. Do not mark ready by simply skipping catalog initialization on roles that require it. Check downstream role/API tests, `mix q` and isolated suites after resolving. This issue tracks the startup blocker, not a new serving product feature.

comments.text: Root cause corrected in 8274d53a6. Jido.Discovery.init_async scans loaded application modules and Code.ensure_loaded?(EXLA.NIF) exits code 137 on this macOS host even when EXLA runtime:false; the kill merely coincided with LLMDB.load. Confirmed standalone LLMDB.Loader.load/1 and LLMDB.load/1 complete successfully without Jido, and standalone Jido startup dies without LLMDB when EXLA is packaged. Native deps now platform-specific: macOS EMLX, Linux EXLA, other platforms no native package; auto-start remains disabled. Jido dev process survived 2.5s with macOS EMLX. Default role tests: 2 property + 51 ExUnit tests passed across application, router, roles and serving dependency/role tests. mix q passed. Mac lockfile excludes EXLA; Linux build must run mix deps.get. No push/merge.

title: [zaq-za4.22] Prevent unsafe EXLA NIF load on macOS startup
